about: Discovery sources for the veteran resource guide: where new or updated listings can come from, how each is read, and what it has yielded. The sources behind already-published records are tracked separately and automatically in data/mining/source-ledger.json. Status: active (used in the pipeline), benchmark (counts used to measure coverage, no listings), manual (read by a person or assistant, then recorded as a harvest file), to_verify (named here, not yet opened), needs_owner (would need an account, key or payment, which is the owner's decision), rejected (too old or not official). See docs/MINING.md.

sources.name: VA facilities by state (FY2021 NCVAS state summaries)
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, National Center for Veterans Analysis and Statistics
sources.yields: Five rows (cemeteries, VBA regional offices, inpatient sites, Vet Centers, outpatient sites), one count column per state. No names, addresses or phones.
sources.notes: Used only as a yardstick in the coverage report: how many VA sites a state has against how many VA location records the guide lists. CC0. One column is misspelled at the source ('wisonson' for Wisconsin); the fetcher maps it.

sources.name: VA Facilities API (Lighthouse)
sources.yields: Every VA medical center, clinic, Vet Center, benefits office and cemetery with address, phone and hours.
sources.notes: The only complete per-facility source. Travis registered a free sandbox key and stores it as the repository secret VA_FACILITIES_API_KEY; the monthly workflow reads it from there and calls the sandbox host. To move to production, set the repository variable VA_FACILITIES_API_BASE to the production URL (or swap url and fallback_url here). The key is sent only in a request header and never written anywhere. Without the secret, the run records this source as skipped. Snapshots record which environment answered; sandbox data is a benchmark and is checked against production or the facility's own page before any listing is published.

sources.name: VA Find Locations and each health system's contact page
sources.yields: The locator itself loads by script and returns no list to a page reader. Each health system's 'contact us' page prints its medical center address, local and toll-free phones and a last-updated date.
sources.notes: The old directory address (va.gov/directory/guide/fac_list_by_state.cfm) now opens the same script-loaded locator.

sources.name: VA SSVF provider intake list, FY26
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Homeless Programs Office
sources.yields: Every SSVF grantee with counties served and intake phones.
sources.notes: Already projected to data/public/ssvf-intake-fy26.json and used by every full county edition. Recheck when VA posts the FY27 list.

sources.name: Each state veterans agency's county or regional service officer directory
sources.yields: One veterans contact per county: office, phone, address, hours.
sources.notes: One source per state; the exact pages are the source_url of every office record and are listed with their review dates in data/mining/source-ledger.json, which is the recheck queue.

sources.name: Arkansas Department of Veterans Affairs: VSO, DVSO, CVSO Directory
sources.yields: All 75 counties with each County Veterans Service Officer's phone and hours; addresses are printed but do not survive text extraction.
sources.notes: Linked as 'Click here to view the full directory' from the department's veteran services map, whose county panels load by script. The file name carries its date; a newer directory gets a new file name, so recheck the map page for the link.

sources.name: State veterans homes
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs and state veterans agencies
sources.yields: Each state veterans home with address, phone and admissions contact.
sources.notes: Next layer after county offices. Use each state veterans agency's own homes page; a national association list is a secondary directory (level D) and only a lead.

sources.name: VA-accredited veterans service organizations
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Office of General Counsel
sources.yields: Recognized organizations that can file claims. Individual representatives are named people and are not published.
sources.notes: The guide already links VA's accreditation search as a national card (va-accredited-help).

sources.name: Civil legal aid programs
sources.yields: Application helpline, hours and counties served.
sources.notes: Read from each program's own apply or contact page; recorded per state in data/source/states/<code>.json.

sources.name: ILRU directory of Centers for Independent Living
sources.publisher: ILRU (Independent Living Research Utilization), national CIL directory
sources.yields: Each center's offices, phones, website and counties served, one page per state (replace the state code at the end of the address).
sources.notes: The national directory used by every full county edition.

sources.name: State long-term care ombudsman programs
sources.publisher: State ombudsman offices; National Long-Term Care Ombudsman Resource Center
sources.yields: Regional ombudsman contacts with counties. The resource center hosts each state's residents' rights brochure and poster (2026 editions under /wp-content/uploads/2026/05/).
sources.notes: Arkansas's brochure lists all eight regions with every county and a phone for each group. Check the same folder for other states whose ombudsman maps load by script.

sources.name: MassGIS: VA Healthcare
sources.yields: Massachusetts VA hospitals and clinics with address and phone (shapefile). MassGIS says the addresses came from VA's own locator.
sources.notes: Published July 3, 2026. Massachusetts only; a lead to confirm against VA's own pages.

sources.name: GOV.UK foreign travel advice: getting help (per country)
sources.yields: Each country's emergency numbers, with a page date.
sources.notes: Used for every country page in data/world/countries.json.

sources.name: HIFLD Open: Veterans Health Administration Medical Facilities (archived copy)
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Homeland Security (HIFLD), archived by the Data Rescue Project
sources.notes: Its own description dates the records to 2007, and HIFLD Open is no longer live. Not used.

sources.name: Meta Ad Library (public ads on Facebook and Instagram)
sources.yields: Active ads matching a search term, with advertiser, headline, text, start date and destination. Opens and searches without signing in; results load by script, so it is read in a browser, not fetched. Every ad is a lead only (evidence E): a program is listed after its own website is read.
sources.notes: First pass 2026-11-27: 466 ads reviewed across 20 search terms, 42 about veteran programs, 15 of them now listed. Outcomes per ad: data/mining/opportunity-leads/meta-ad-library-2026-11-27.json. See docs/OPPORTUNITIES.md.
